nodes.label: --resume (never pay twice)
nodes.rationale: LinkedIn search pages are re-bought on resume because icypeas page tokens expire.

nodes.label: crawl4ai.google.serp.maps
nodes.rationale: 100 rows per call vs 20 for the routed treg.google.serp.maps; rows complete so no place-details call.

nodes.label: hunter.companies.emails (opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Reserves $0.0245 per domain, so it is opt-in via --paid-emails.

nodes.label: icypeas.companies.search
nodes.rationale: Replaced treg.companies.search in M12 because it can filter by state and city.

nodes.label: icypeas.people.search
nodes.rationale: profileLocation filter gave 20/20 in Texas and paging works, unlike routed treg.people.search (6/10, cursor did not page).

nodes.label: M11 work email & phone finder (find_contact)
nodes.rationale: Never send X-Treg-Route-Verify on the finder: it tried 5 providers, ran past 120 s and cost $0.018.

nodes.norm_label: m4 website deep scrape (crawl_site, extract_contacts, extract_details)
nodes.rationale: Free and runs before any paid lookup; JSON-LD first; bot-checked sites skipped, never worked around.

nodes.norm_label: m8 area coverage (state -> cities -> zip codes)
nodes.rationale: One Maps search caps at 100 places, so saturated cells are re-split.

nodes.label: common.py shared core (treg client, budget, CSV writer, website scrape, suppression)
nodes.norm_label: common.py shared core (treg client, budget, csv writer, website scrape, suppression)
nodes.rationale: Neither scraper imports the other; shared code lives only in common.py.

nodes.label: endpoints.json (endpoint, price, cap per capability)
nodes.rationale: Change providers here only.

nodes.label: treg (tool registry / proxy at treg.to)
nodes.rationale: One token gives access to all paid providers; no LinkedIn/Google login, no browser automation, no CAPTCHA bypass.

nodes.label: Lead Scraper Build Modules (M0-M16 plan)
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 (Google) before Phase 3 (LinkedIn) because Maps listings include phone and website, testing shared enrichment on the easier source first.

nodes.label: orbisearch and tomba excluded from fallback
nodes.norm_label: orbisearch and tomba excluded from fallback
nodes.rationale: orbisearch billed $0.0062 every attempt for a 1.6% hit rate; tomba had 0 hits in 7 tries and 72% of run time, so excluding both makes tier-2 misses free and fast.

nodes.label: Shared enrichment pipeline (cheapest-first)
nodes.rationale: Neither LinkedIn pages nor Google listings show emails, so free website crawl first, then extract, then paid finder, then verify.

nodes.label: Two-tier work email finder (blitzapi then routed finder)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier work email finder (blitzapi then routed finder)
nodes.rationale: Cheap tier first with free misses; routed fallback only for misses, capped at $0.011; no address ever guessed.

nodes.label: M3 LeadWriter, CSV output & resume
nodes.rationale: utf-8-sig and flush per row; phones in international format because Excel shows bare E.164 as 1.51E+10.

nodes.label: Common behaviour C1-C9 (dry-run, max-cost, resume, retry, suppress)
nodes.norm_label: common behaviour c1-c9 (dry-run, max-cost, resume, retry, suppress)

nodes.label: Shared first 12 CSV columns
nodes.rationale: Identical first columns in all three CSVs so files can be stacked later without a merged mode.

nodes.label: Suppression list (suppress.txt)
nodes.rationale: Applied inside the CSV writer so no code path can bypass it.

nodes.label: Budget with parallel calls (reserve cap in flight)
nodes.norm_label: budget with parallel calls (reserve cap in flight)
nodes.rationale: 8 workers each reserving their cap could end a small --max-cost run early, so Treg waits for in-flight calls to settle.

nodes.label: M2 treg client & cost control (call, BudgetReached, estimate)
nodes.norm_label: m2 treg client & cost control (call, budgetreached, estimate)
nodes.rationale: One function is the only way to talk to treg: token, retries, logging and budget in one place.

nodes.label: 180 s client timeout
nodes.rationale: A routed email lookup took 77 s; one with route-verify ran over 120 s.

nodes.label: X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost header rule
nodes.rationale: Routed treg.* endpoints bill misses and default to a $1 cap per call, so the cap is always sent.
